title: The Patents Act, 1970
summary: Excludes from patentability an invention which, in effect, is traditional knowledge or which is an aggregation or duplication of known properties of a traditionally known component or components.
source_url: https://ipindia.gov.in (Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs & Trade Marks — official portal; exact clause URL not verified, verify before production use)
precision: section-level, verified provision text; deep-link not verified

title: The Patents Act, 1970
summary: Excludes plants and animals in whole or any part thereof other than micro-organisms, and essentially biological processes for production or propagation of plants and animals, from patentability.
source_url: https://ipindia.gov.in (official portal; deep-link not verified)
precision: section-level, verified provision text; deep-link not verified

title: The Biological Diversity Act, 2002
section: General framework (access to biological resources and associated knowledge)
summary: Establishes the National Biodiversity Authority and requires prior approval for obtaining biological resources occurring in India and associated traditional knowledge for research, commercial use, or IP applications, with benefit-sharing conditions.
version_date: 2002, as amended by the Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act, 2023
source_url: https://nbaindia.org (National Biodiversity Authority — official portal; exact section not pinpointed)
authority: Government of India / National Biodiversity Authority
precision: act-level; exact section not pinpointed, verify before production use

title: The Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and Rules, 1945
section: Provisions on Ayurvedic, Siddha and Unani drugs (Chapter IV-A and related Schedules)
summary: Distinguishes classical Ayurvedic medicines (formulations described in authoritative texts listed in the First Schedule, manufacturable under a standard licence) from Patent or Proprietary Ayurvedic medicines (novel formulations requiring formula approval before a manufacturing licence is granted).
source_url: https://cdsco.gov.in / https://main.ayush.gov.in (official portals; exact rule numbers not pinpointed)
authority: Government of India / Ministry of AYUSH / CDSCO
precision: act-level summary; exact rule numbers not pinpointed, verify before production use

title: Food Safety and Standards (Health Supplements, Nutraceuticals, Food for Special Dietary Use, Food for Special Medical Purpose, Functional Food and Novel Food) Regulations, 2016
summary: Governs health supplements and nutraceutical products, including Ayurveda Aahar formulations that are positioned as food rather than drugs, setting composition, labelling and claim requirements distinct from the Drugs and Cosmetics Act regime.
source_url: https://fssai.gov.in (official portal; exact regulation clause not pinpointed)
authority: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
precision: regulation-level summary; exact clause not pinpointed, verify before production use

title: Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999
summary: Provides for registration and protection of geographical indications, relevant where an Ayurvedic product's reputation or characteristics are essentially attributable to a specific geographical origin (e.g. region-specific herbal preparations).
source_url: https://ipindia.gov.in (official GI Registry portal; exact section not pinpointed)
precision: act-level summary; verify before production use

title: WTO Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS)
summary: Sets baseline patentability criteria (novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability) and permits members to exclude certain subject matter, including plants and animals other than micro-organisms and essentially biological processes, from patentability.
source_url: https://www.wto.org (official TRIPS text portal)
precision: article-level, verified provision text

title: Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)
summary: One of the CBD's three objectives is the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from the utilization of genetic resources, forming the basis for national ABS frameworks worldwide.
source_url: https://www.cbd.int (official CBD portal)
authority: Secretariat of the Convention on Biological Diversity
precision: framework-level, verified provision text

title: Nagoya Protocol on Access to Genetic Resources and the Fair and Equitable Sharing of Benefits Arising from their Utilization
summary: Supplements the CBD with detailed procedural obligations on prior informed consent and mutually agreed terms for access to genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge, including in traditional medicine contexts.
source_url: https://www.cbd.int/abs (official Nagoya Protocol portal)
authority: Secretariat of the Convention on Biological Diversity
precision: framework-level, verified provision text

title: Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (TKDL)
summary: A joint CSIR-Ministry of AYUSH database that documents codified traditional knowledge from Ayurveda, Unani, Siddha and Yoga texts in a searchable format, made available to select international patent offices (e.g. EPO, USPTO, and others under access agreements) as prior art to prevent misappropriation of traditional knowledge through patents.
source_url: https://www.tkdl.res.in (official TKDL portal; underlying database itself is access-restricted, not publicly browsable)
authority: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) / Ministry of AYUSH
precision: database is confidential/restricted-access; this prototype does not connect to real TKDL data and only demonstrates the reference workflow

title: WIPO Intergovernmental Committee on Intellectual Property and Genetic Resources, Traditional Knowledge and Folklore (IGC)
summary: A WIPO forum negotiating international legal instrument(s) on the protection of traditional knowledge, traditional cultural expressions and genetic resources; as of the last verified review no single binding global IP treaty for traditional knowledge protection had been concluded (a 2024 WIPO Treaty on IP, Genetic Resources and Associated Traditional Knowledge addresses disclosure obligations specifically).
source_url: https://www.wipo.int/tk (official WIPO portal)
precision: framework/status summary; verify current negotiation status before production use

title: The Trade Marks Act, 1999
section: General framework (registration and protection of trademarks)
summary: Governs registration and protection of trademarks in India, including product/brand names and logos used for Ayurvedic products, administered by the Trade Marks Registry under the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM).
source_url: https://ipindia.gov.in (Trade Marks Registry — official portal; exact section not pinpointed)
authority: Government of India / Trade Marks Registry
precision: act-level summary; verify exact section before production use

title: The Copyright Act, 1957
section: General framework (literary, artistic and other original works)
summary: Governs copyright protection for original literary, artistic and other works in India; relevant to original written/illustrated material created around an Ayurvedic product (packaging text, manuals), while ancient classical Ayurvedic texts themselves are generally in the public domain due to their age.
source_url: https://copyright.gov.in (Copyright Office — official portal; exact section not pinpointed)
precision: act-level summary; verify exact section before production use

title: The Designs Act, 2000
summary: Governs registration of industrial designs in India — the visual, non-functional features of shape, configuration, pattern or ornamentation applied to an article — relevant to distinctive product/packaging shapes for Ayurvedic products.
source_url: https://ipindia.gov.in (Designs Wing — official portal; exact section not pinpointed)
authority: Government of India / Patent Office (Designs Wing)
precision: act-level summary; verify exact section before production use

title: Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Act, 2001
section: General framework (plant variety registration and farmers' rights)
summary: India's sui generis plant variety protection regime — an alternative to patenting for plant varieties, as permitted under TRIPS Article 27.3(b) — relevant where an Ayurvedic product relies on a specific cultivated medicinal plant variety. Also protects farmers' rights over traditional varieties.
source_url: https://plantauthority.gov.in (PPV&FR Authority — official portal; exact section not pinpointed)
authority: Government of India / Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Authority
precision: act-level summary; verify exact section before production use

title: The Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954
section: General framework (prohibition of objectionable/misleading drug advertisements)
summary: Prohibits advertisements that make misleading claims about a drug's efficacy, including claims of magical or miraculous properties — directly relevant to how classical, proprietary or new Ayurvedic formulations may be marketed and advertised in India.
source_url: https://main.ayush.gov.in / https://cdsco.gov.in (official portals; exact section not pinpointed)
precision: act-level summary; verify exact section before production use

title: Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011
summary: Sets mandatory labelling declarations for pre-packaged commodities in India — net quantity, manufacturer/packer details, maximum retail price, month/year of manufacture — applicable to packaged Ayurvedic products regardless of their drug/cosmetic/food classification.
source_url: https://consumeraffairs.nic.in (Department of Consumer Affairs — official portal; exact rule not pinpointed)
authority: Government of India / Department of Consumer Affairs
precision: rules-level summary; exact rule number not pinpointed, verify before production use

title: The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006
section: General framework (establishing FSSAI and the food-safety regulatory scheme)
summary: The parent statute establishing the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) and the overall food-safety regulatory framework under which the 2016 health-supplement/nutraceutical regulations (see IN-FSSAI-2016) were subsequently made.
source_url: https://fssai.gov.in (official portal; exact section not pinpointed)
authority: Government of India / Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
precision: act-level summary; verify exact section before production use

title: Convention Establishing the World Intellectual Property Organization
section: General framework (establishment and mandate of WIPO)
summary: Establishes WIPO as the United Nations specialized agency responsible for administering major international IP treaties (patents, trademarks, designs, copyright) and promoting international IP cooperation, including the treaties this corpus references (PCT, Madrid Protocol, Hague Agreement, Berne and Paris Conventions).
source_url: https://www.wipo.int (official WIPO portal)
precision: framework-level, verified provision text

title: Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT)
summary: Allows an applicant to file a single international patent application that has effect in multiple PCT member states (including India), streamlining — but not replacing — the need to eventually seek and obtain a patent in each country's national/regional patent office.
source_url: https://www.wipo.int/pct (official WIPO PCT portal)
precision: framework-level, verified provision text

title: Madrid Protocol (Madrid System for the International Registration of Marks)
summary: Allows a trademark owner to file a single international application, based on a national/regional application or registration, seeking protection in multiple member countries; India acceded to the Madrid Protocol in 2013.
source_url: https://www.wipo.int/madrid (official WIPO Madrid System portal)
precision: framework-level summary; verify current India-specific accession details before production use

title: Hague Agreement Concerning the International Registration of Industrial Designs (Geneva Act, 1999)
summary: Allows an applicant to file a single international application seeking design protection in multiple member countries, administered by WIPO's International Bureau, relevant to product/packaging designs seeking protection beyond India.
source_url: https://www.wipo.int/hague (official WIPO Hague System portal)
precision: framework-level summary; verify current India-specific membership status before production use

title: Berne Convention for the Protection of Literary and Artistic Works
section: General framework (automatic international copyright protection, minimum standards)
summary: The foundational international copyright treaty; member countries must grant automatic copyright protection (no registration required) to works from other member countries and meet certain minimum standards of protection, including minimum term of life of the author plus 50 years.
source_url: https://www.wipo.int/treaties/en/ip/berne (official WIPO Berne Convention portal)
precision: framework-level, verified provision text

title: Paris Convention for the Protection of Industrial Property
section: General framework (national treatment and right of priority)
summary: The foundational international treaty for patents, trademarks and industrial designs; establishes 'national treatment' (foreign applicants get the same protection as nationals) and a 'right of priority' — 12 months for patents, 6 months for trademarks and designs, to file in other member countries claiming the first filing date.
source_url: https://www.wipo.int/treaties/en/ip/paris (official WIPO Paris Convention portal)
precision: framework-level, verified provision text

title: International Convention for the Protection of New Varieties of Plants (UPOV Convention, 1991 Act)
summary: An international framework for protecting new plant varieties through breeders' rights, administered by UPOV (headquartered alongside WIPO in Geneva). India is not a UPOV member; India instead adopted its own sui generis regime, the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Act, 2001 (see IN-PPVFR-2001), as its TRIPS-compliant alternative.
source_url: https://www.upov.int (official UPOV portal)
authority: International Union for the Protection of New Varieties of Plants (UPOV)
precision: framework-level summary; verify current membership list before production use
